question: How often must a bank carry out KYC periodic updation for high-risk, medium-risk and low-risk customers under the Commercial Banks KYC Directions, 2025?
reference_answer: At least once every two years for high-risk customers, once every eight years for medium-risk customers, and once every ten years for low-risk customers, from the date of account opening or last KYC updation.
notes: All three intervals required (2/8/10 years). Page 41, para 42.

question: Under the KYC Master Direction, 2016, what risk categories must REs place customers in?
reference_answer: Low, medium and high-risk categories, based on the RE's own assessment and risk perception.
notes: Three categories, risk-based approach. Page 21, para 12(a).

question: How must banks classify their entire investment portfolio under the 2023 Investment Portfolio Directions?
reference_answer: Under three categories - Held to Maturity (HTM), Available for Sale (AFS) and Fair Value through Profit and Loss (FVTPL) - with Held for Trading (HFT) as a separate sub-category within FVTPL, excluding investments in own subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates.
notes: Three categories plus the HFT sub-category. Page 15.

question: What rank and reporting constraints apply to the CISO under the IT Governance Directions, 2023?
reference_answer: The CISO must be a senior-level executive, preferably in the rank of a General Manager or equivalent, must not have any direct reporting relationship with the Head of the IT Function, and must not be given any business targets.
notes: Three elements: senior/GM rank, no reporting to Head of IT, no business targets. Page 17.

question: Can a card-issuer breach the sanctioned credit limit without the cardholder's explicit consent under the 2022 Credit Card and Debit Card Directions?
reference_answer: No. The credit limit as sanctioned and advised must not be breached at any point in time without seeking explicit consent from the cardholder.
notes: Explicit-consent rule, no exceptions stated. Page 8.

question: What consent does an Account Aggregator need before providing services to a customer?
reference_answer: The Account Aggregator must provide services based on the customer's explicit consent, backed by appropriate agreements or authorisations.
notes: Explicit consent, per the duties clause. Page 8.

question: How is a guarantor's liability treated under the Wilful Defaulters Directions, 2024?
reference_answer: As per Section 128 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, the liability of the guarantor is coextensive with that of the principal debtor unless it is otherwise provided by the contract.
notes: Must cite coextensive liability and Section 128 of the Indian Contract Act. Page 16.

question: Where must an RE store digital lending data, and what is the rule for data processed outside India?
reference_answer: All data must be stored only on servers located within India; if data is processed outside India it must be deleted from servers outside India and brought back to India within 24 hours of processing.
notes: India-only storage plus the 24-hour repatriation rule. Page 12.

question: Which IT outsourcing arrangements do the 2023 Outsourcing Directions apply to?
reference_answer: They apply to Material Outsourcing of Information Technology (IT) Services arrangements entered into by regulated entities.
notes: Scope is material IT outsourcing arrangements only. Page 7.

question: Is there a cap on the amount in a dispute that can be taken to the RBI Ombudsman?
reference_answer: No - there is no limit on the amount in a dispute that can be brought before the Ombudsman. Compensation is separately capped: up to Rs 20 lakh for consequential loss plus up to Rs 1 lakh for loss of time, expenses and harassment.
notes: No cap on the dispute amount itself; compensation caps are separate. Page 5, clause 8(2).

question: What Free Full Credit Report policy must a Credit Information Company maintain?
reference_answer: A CIC must have board-approved policies on making available the Free Full Credit Report (FFCR).
notes: Board-approved FFCR policy. Page 5, para 7(i).

question: Who reports the liquidity risk profile to a bank's ALCO under the ALM Directions, 2025?
reference_answer: The ALM Support Group, consisting of operating staff, is responsible for analysing, monitoring and reporting the liquidity risk profile to the ALCO.
notes: ALM Support Group (operating staff), not the ALCO itself. Page 14, para 28.

question: What is the Minimum Retention Requirement meant to ensure under the 2021 Securitisation Directions?
reference_answer: It ensures that originators have a continuing stake in the performance of the securitised assets, so that they carry out the necessary diligence on the assets they securitise.
notes: Continuing stake of the originator in asset performance. Page 10, para 12 (B. Minimum Retention Requirement).

question: For how long must a PPI issuer keep a log of all transactions?
reference_answer: At least ten years.
notes: Exactly 10 years (minimum). No tolerance. Page 7, clause 6.3.

question: What is the total priority sector lending target for scheduled commercial banks under the 2020 PSL Directions?
reference_answer: 40 per cent of ANBC or CEOBE, whichever is higher.
notes: 40% is the number; denominator ANBC-or-CEOBE-whichever-higher is the full form. Accept 40 per cent alone as correct, prefer full form. Page 5, para 5.

question: What is the agriculture priority sector target, including the sub-target for Small and Marginal Farmers, under the 2020 PSL Directions?
reference_answer: 18 per cent of ANBC or CEOBE, whichever is higher, of which a target of 10 per cent is prescribed for Small and Marginal Farmers.
notes: Both numbers required: 18% agriculture, 10% SMF within it. Partial credit for one of two. Page 5, para 5.

question: What are the monthly load, yearly load and outstanding limits for a small (minimum-detail) PPI?
reference_answer: Amount loaded during any month must not exceed Rs 10,000; total loaded during the financial year must not exceed Rs 1,20,000; amount outstanding at any point in time must not exceed Rs 10,000 (monthly debits are likewise capped at Rs 10,000).
notes: All three (ideally four) figures: 10,000/month load, 1,20,000/year load, 10,000 outstanding, 10,000 monthly debit. Partial credit for 2-3. Page 10, clause 9.1.

question: What is the maximum compensation the Ombudsman can award for consequential loss?
reference_answer: Up to Rs 20 lakh for consequential loss, in addition to up to Rs 1 lakh for loss of the complainant's time, expenses incurred and harassment or mental anguish.
notes: Rs 20 lakh is the consequential-loss cap; the Rs 1 lakh is a separate head - do not conflate. Page 5, clause 8(2).

question: After how many days of continuous overdue interest or principal is a term loan classified as an NPA under the IRAC Directions, 2025?
reference_answer: More than 90 days.
notes: Threshold is more than 90 days overdue. Page 18, para 42(1).

question: What dividend payout ratio can an eligible NBFC-P2P declare?
reference_answer: Up to a dividend payout ratio of 50 per cent for NBFC-P2Ps meeting the eligibility criteria; there is no ceiling for eligible NBFC-P2Ps that do not accept public funds.
notes: Primary number is 50%; the no-public-funds carve-out is bonus. Page 7.

question: What are the one-time and annual membership fee caps for a Credit Information Company charging its member CIs?
reference_answer: The one-time membership fee must not exceed Rs 10,000 each, and annual fees must not exceed Rs 5,000 each.
notes: Both figures required: 10,000 one-time, 5,000 annual. Page 8, para 14(1)-(2).

question: What are the per-transaction and per-month limits on cross-border outward transactions using Rupee-denominated PPIs?
reference_answer: A per-transaction limit not exceeding Rs 10,000 and a per-month limit not exceeding Rs 50,000, enabled only on the explicit request of the PPI holder.
notes: Both figures: 10,000 per transaction, 50,000 per month. Page 9.

question: As of 31 March 2025, what was the total priority sector lending target for scheduled commercial banks?
reference_answer: 40 per cent of ANBC or CEOBE, whichever is higher, under the 2020 PSL Directions - which were withdrawn with effect from 1 April 2025.
notes: As-of date is the day before the 2020 Directions were withdrawn (cover page: 'Withdrawn w.e.f April 01, 2025'). Baseline runs with temporal_filter off; the as_of_date is honoured from Phase 3.

question: As of January 2023, what maximum compensation could the Ombudsman award for consequential loss?
reference_answer: Up to Rs 20 lakh under the Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021.
notes: Consolidated Scheme text is dated 2022-08-05 (<= as_of). Rs 20 lakh.

question: As of mid-2022, what were the load limits for a small PPI?
reference_answer: Rs 10,000 per month and Rs 1,20,000 per financial year, with Rs 10,000 outstanding at any time, under the PPI Directions, 2021.
notes: PPI Directions issued 2021-08-27 (<= as_of). Same figures as q0017 but framed temporally.

question: As of early 2017, what consent rule applied to Account Aggregators serving customers?
reference_answer: An Account Aggregator must provide services to a customer based on the customer's explicit consent.
notes: AA Directions issued 2016-09-02 (<= as_of). Explicit consent.

question: As of August 2024, how was a guarantor's liability treated in wilful defaulter cases?
reference_answer: Coextensive with that of the principal debtor as per Section 128 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, unless otherwise provided by the contract.
notes: Directions issued 2024-07-30 (<= as_of). Section 128 coextensive liability.

question: As of end-2023, how much experience qualified as 'substantial IT expertise' for an IT Strategy Committee member?
reference_answer: A minimum of seven years of experience in managing information systems and/or leading, guiding technology and cybersecurity initiatives or projects.
notes: 7 years. Directions issued 2023-11-07 (<= as_of). Page 8, footnote 9.

question: Do the Commercial Banks KYC Directions, 2025 and the NBFC KYC Directions, 2025 prescribe the same KYC periodic-updation intervals?
reference_answer: Yes - both prescribe identical intervals: every two years for high-risk customers, every eight years for medium-risk customers and every ten years for low-risk customers.
notes: Both gold passages required. Answer must say they are the same AND give the three intervals; missing either part is partial credit.

question: Is customer risk categorisation the same under the KYC Master Direction, 2016 and the Commercial Banks KYC Directions, 2025?
reference_answer: Yes - both require the same three categories (low, medium and high risk) based on the entity's assessment and risk perception.
notes: Must cite both documents; describing only one side is partial credit.

question: Under the 2020 PSL Directions, is the total priority sector target larger than the agriculture target, and by how much?
reference_answer: Yes - the total target is 40 per cent and the agriculture target is 18 per cent (both of ANBC or CEOBE, whichever is higher), so the total is larger by 22 percentage points.
notes: Require both figures (40% and 18%) and the difference (22 percentage points). Page 5, para 5.

question: How does the Ombudsman's consequential-loss compensation cap compare with the cap for loss of time and harassment?
reference_answer: Consequential loss is capped at Rs 20 lakh while loss of time, expenses and mental anguish is capped at Rs 1 lakh - the consequential-loss cap is twenty times larger.
notes: Rs 20 lakh vs Rs 1 lakh (20x). Both caps are additional to each other, not alternatives. Page 5.

question: Which PPI cross-border limit is larger - the per-transaction cap or the monthly cap - and by what factor?
reference_answer: The monthly cap is larger: Rs 50,000 per month versus Rs 10,000 per transaction, i.e. five times the per-transaction cap.
notes: 50,000 vs 10,000; factor 5x. Page 9.

question: What data-localisation rule applies under the Digital Lending Directions, 2025, and which parties does it bind?
reference_answer: Data must be stored only on servers located within India, and data processed outside India must be deleted there and brought back within 24 hours of processing. The obligations bind the regulated entity together with its Lending Service Provider and the Digital Lending Apps/Platforms involved, which include both the RE's own apps and those operated by the LSP.
notes: Two hops: the storage rule (p.12) and the RE/LSP/DLA definitions showing who is bound (p.5). Answer covering only the storage rule is partial credit.

question: What total PSL target applies to scheduled commercial banks under the 2020 Directions, and how is ANBC defined?
reference_answer: The total target is 40 per cent of ANBC or CEOBE, whichever is higher. ANBC denotes the outstanding Bank Credit in India as prescribed in item VI of Form A under Section 42(2) of the RBI Act, 1934, computed per para 6 of the Directions (bank credit in India less specified adjustments).
notes: Two hops across pages: target (p.5) and the ANBC definition (p.7). Both parts required for full credit.

question: When may a complainant go to the Ombudsman under the 2021 Scheme, and what is the maximum consequential-loss compensation?
reference_answer: When the regulated entity rejected the complaint wholly or partly and the complainant is unsatisfied, or there was no reply within 30 days - and the complaint must be made within one year of the reply (or within one year and 30 days of the complaint if no reply). Maximum consequential-loss compensation is Rs 20 lakh.
notes: Two hops: filing conditions/deadline (p.7) and the compensation cap (p.5). Both parts required.

question: What rank must the CISO hold and what experience counts as 'substantial IT expertise' under the IT Governance Directions, 2023?
reference_answer: The CISO must be a senior-level executive, preferably in the rank of a General Manager or equivalent. Substantial IT expertise means a minimum of seven years of experience in managing information systems and/or leading or guiding technology and cybersecurity initiatives or projects.
notes: Two hops across pages: CISO rank (p.17) and the seven-years definition (p.8, footnote 9). Both parts required.
